solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Back at last, decided to watch Puss in Boots

indicators.note: 'at last' points to the final letter of each word that follows
going back means reading the collected letters from end to start

blocks.note: the closing letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Someone finally makes up their mind to go to the pantomime Puss in Boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puss in Boots' reads as one title, but the clue splits after 'Puss': the last letters of 'decided to watch Puss' read backwards give SHOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Shod is the old past participle of shoe, describing someone wearing footwear, so a person in boots is shod.

clue.text: Speed along, changing his rank in sect

indicators.note: changing the letters around means putting them in a new order

blocks.note: to hare is to run very fast
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A member of a religious group is hurried along to a new position within it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests promotion within a sect, but the letters of 'his rank' simply rearrange into the name of the god.
explanation.definitionFit: Hare Krishna is the popular name of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness, a religious movement known for chanting.

clue.text: Chipper, contribute two pounds and nothing more

blocks.note: to contribute is to give
L is the abbreviation for a pound, twice
nothing is zero, a round O, with nothing more after it

explanation.surface: A cheerful appeal to chip in a couple of pounds and not a penny extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chipper' looks like the adjective meaning cheerful, but it is a noun: one who chips, here a sculptor chipping stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine Renaissance sculptor worked in marble and stone, and a sculptor chips away at his material with a chisel.

clue.text: Solo one takes up this credit, getting oil converted into power

indicators.note: something converted has been changed into a new form, so these letters are reordered
going into something means being placed inside it

blocks.note: might is strength or power
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lone pilot takes this aircraft up, burning fuel for engine power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solo one takes up this' is a whole-phrase definition: the aircraft is typically flown by one person alone. The inserted letters go in after the second letter of the power word.
explanation.definitionFit: A microlight is a very small, light aircraft, often a single seater, so one person alone flies it up.

clue.text: President died in house abroad

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for died
maison is French for house

explanation.surface: A head of state passed away in a residence overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' asks for a foreign word; the French MAISON takes D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth President of the United States, one of the founding fathers.

clue.text: Pass current format for new opening of major novel

indicators.note: making something new means giving these letters a fresh order
an opening is the start, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: a col is a mountain pass
DC is direct current
taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A publisher approves a new format for the launch of a big novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay pieces do not respect the word breaks: the first word ends a letter early, and the second word's opening C comes from the abbreviation for current.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella Gibbons's 1932 comic book about a gloomy Sussex farm is a well-known English work of fiction.

clue.text: Give up, losing rating for working without pause

indicators.note: losing one thing drops it from the word
one thing for another means one takes the other's place

blocks.note: to abandon is to give up
an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone quits because their score was lowered for toiling non-stop.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a sailor below officer rank; swapping ON in for AB at the front turns ABANDON into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on and on means continuing endlessly, with no break or rest at any point.

clue.text: Intending to monitor bar area

indicators.note: to bar something is to shut it out, so it is removed

blocks.note: a goanna is an Australian monitor lizard
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Someone planning to keep an eye on a pub's drinking area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monitor' reads as a verb, but it is the lizard. One of the two As goes, leaving the informal contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Gonna is casual speech for going to, which expresses a plan or future intention.

clue.text: Columns of data small computer doesn’t finish

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a tablet is a small handheld computer

explanation.surface: A little device fails to complete displaying a spreadsheet's columns.
explanation.walkthrough: The small computer is cut short by its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A table is data arranged in rows and columns, as in a spreadsheet or statistical report.

clue.text: Fruit badly stored in Moorish city

indicators.note: something stored in a place is kept inside it

blocks.note: ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated
the Spanish city was the last Moorish stronghold

explanation.surface: Produce kept poorly in a storehouse in a southern Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: Granada, home of the Alhambra, was ruled by the Moors until 1492; ILL goes in before its final A.
explanation.definitionFit: The granadilla is the edible fruit of a passion flower, a close relative of the passion fruit.

clue.text: Fail to acknowledge name in advance

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
a sub is an advance on wages

explanation.surface: Someone forgets to credit a person's name ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a sub is money paid ahead of wages; N goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is to ignore or rebuff them deliberately, pointedly refusing to greet them.

clue.text: Hurry to get these fish on

definitions.text: Hurry to get these fish on

blocks.clueFragment: Hurry to get these fish on
blocks.note: surface: an angler rushing to bait or land a catch
setter: the flat fish are also footwear, and putting them on is an idiom for hurrying

explanation.surface: A fishmonger or angler urged to be quick about getting the catch ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get your skates on' is the British idiom for hurry up; the same word names a flat fish, so the fish are what you put on.
explanation.definitionFit: These flat rays share a name with ice or roller footwear, which the idiom tells you to put on quickly.

clue.text: Spy may take this and come east in disguise

indicators.note: a disguise changes appearance, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An agent might adopt a cover and come over from the East in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cold War picture of coming from the East hides a single letter for the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret agents are given an alias for use in messages and operations, a word hiding their real identity.

clue.text: Improve hard lesson prepared for Felix

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked into shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to mend is to repair or make better
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tough lesson has been got ready for a pupil named Felix, or a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felix' looks like a pupil's name, but it is the composer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Felix Mendelssohn was the German Romantic composer of the Italian Symphony and the Wedding March.

clue.text: Does she give both hands to soldier?

blocks.note: a GI is an American soldier
right and left, R and L, are both hands

explanation.surface: A question whether a woman gives her hands in marriage to a serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: The two hands are right and left; they come after the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl is a female child or young woman, whom one would refer to with the pronoun she.

clue.text: 1066 Pevensey event — no resistance in contested region

indicators.note: having no such thing means it is taken away

blocks.note: in 1066 William's Normans came ashore at Pevensey in Sussex
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: The Norman landing of 1066 met no opposition in a disputed territory.
explanation.walkthrough: Pevensey is the Sussex beach where the Norman invasion landed before the Battle of Hastings; without its R the phrase becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: No-man's-land is the strip between opposing trenches or borders that neither side controls, claimed by both.

clue.text: Cavalryman engages a paid club entertainer

indicators.note: to engage can mean to take in or hold, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a lancer is a mounted soldier armed with a lance
taken as written
PD is the abbreviation for paid

explanation.surface: A cavalry soldier hires a professional performer for the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engages' reads as hiring, and the surface keeps that sense, but here it means holding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap dancer performs erotic dances close to customers in nightclubs, so is a type of club performer.

clue.text: Completely dismissed in audition

indicators.note: an audition is heard, so the answer is judged by its sound

blocks.note: to dismiss something is to throw it out

explanation.surface: An actor is entirely rejected at a tryout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' paints a stage casting, but it simply means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout means in every part or for the whole duration, so it fits entirely or totally.

clue.text: Grand family of babies sparkle

blocks.note: G is short for grand, a thousand
a litter is the young born to an animal at one time

explanation.surface: A proud relative says her grandchildren's family sparkles.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars, abbreviated G.
explanation.definitionFit: To glitter is to shine with bright shimmering flashes of light, as a sequin or jewel does.

clue.text: Serious offence requires time to think

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to reason is to think logically

explanation.surface: A grave crime needs careful thought before judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: The link 'requires' joins the definition to T followed by the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or sovereign is among the gravest crimes, historically punishable by death.

clue.text: Ask out loud for something to eat

indicators.note: said out loud, a word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: to pray is to ask earnestly, as in 'pray tell'

explanation.surface: Someone requests food, saying it plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as asking for food; the definition is the food itself, an animal hunted and eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Prey is an animal hunted and killed by a predator for food, its next meal.

clue.text: Leading celebrities plump for one who is no influencer

blocks.note: plump means fat
the A-list are the top celebrities

explanation.surface: Top stars choose someone without social media sway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump for' looks like a phrasal verb meaning choose; here 'plump' is the adjective and it goes in front. 'Influencer' suggests social media, but the definition means someone who believes they cannot change events.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatalist believes that everything is predetermined, so they think their own actions make no difference to outcomes.

clue.text: Force opposing exploiter of children

blocks.note: F is the physics symbol for force
agin is dialect for against

explanation.surface: A campaign force stands against someone who abuses young people.
explanation.walkthrough: AGIN is an old dialect form of against, familiar in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's Oliver Twist, Fagin runs a gang of young pickpockets who steal for his profit.

clue.text: Keep in drawer

blocks.note: first meaning: the strongest central stronghold of a castle
second meaning: one who draws or pulls something along behind

explanation.surface: Store something in a chest's sliding compartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' sounds like furniture but means one who draws, that is pulls; 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the castle noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle keep is its great fortified tower, and a vehicle hauling another by rope is a tower.

clue.text: Go by turns extremely expressionless and faint

indicators.note: the extremes are the ends, so only the outermost letters are kept
what turns round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the first and last letters
a faint colour is pale

explanation.surface: Someone alternately goes blank-faced and swoons as they pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By turns' reads as a phrase meaning alternately, but 'by' belongs to the definition and 'turns' tells you to run the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes or slips away, just as days are said to go by.

clue.text: During interval, women’s rude stare

indicators.note: something happening during a period falls within it

blocks.note: a gap is an interval
W is the abbreviation for women, with the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: At the break, the ladies give someone an impolite look.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is read as 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To gawp is to gape stupidly or rudely, and it can also be used as a noun for such a gaping look.

clue.text: Negotiator gives drama lessons, except one

indicators.note: except means leaving out, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: one who gives drama lessons trains an actor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dealmaker coaches performers, with a single exception.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read as the three-word idea 'trains actor', from which the Roman one is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A transactor is one who conducts business dealings, arranging deals between parties just as a bargainer does.

clue.text: One in a growing business, a baby-minder?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who works at a garden centre raising young plants
second meaning, whimsical: a man working in a room for small children

explanation.surface: A worker in an expanding company doubles as a childminder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growing business' suggests a thriving firm, but it is horticulture; the question mark flags the jokey second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant nursery raises seedlings for sale, while a nursery is also where infants are cared for.

clue.text: Hard work, scrubbing good skin

indicators.note: to scrub can mean to cancel or wipe out, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a grind is tedious hard work
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Scouring a tough hide takes real effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrubbing' suggests cleaning, but it means cancelling, as in scrubbing a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Rind is the tough outer layer of fruit, cheese or bacon, its protective covering.
